units.translation: an interjection used by those grieving deeply, in the manuscripts of the tragedians often written ὀττοτοῖ [ototoi] and with the incorrect accent ὀτοτοί or όττοτοί against the rule of Apollonius in Bekker's Anecdota p. 588, 25 (from which the reading ότοτοί on p. 537, 33 should be corrected). There also existed a disyllabic form τοτοῖ [tototoi], which the tragedians sometimes attached to the trisyllabic form, or more often made more intense by repeating το [to], as in ὀτοτοτοῖ στέναξον [otototoi, groan] in Euripides Hercules Furens 875 and much longer in Trojan Women 1287. On all these see Thesaurus vol. 5 p. 2335. Examples from Aeschylus are
in a dochmiac verse. Thus from the copy, for ὁ το τοῦ μάταν [o to tou matan], which is thus in M, but in the antistrophe (v. 274) correctly ὁ τοτο τοῦ φίλων [o toto tou philon].
in anapaests, thus from the copy, for βασιλεύς [king]. Thus Blomfield for ότοτοτοῖ [otototoi].

and 1051 in strophe and antistrophe before iambic dimeters (some copies have ότοτοῖ [ototoi]), where more probable is ἰοῖ οἰοῖ [ioi oioi], which Weilius conjectured, as at v. 1067 before an iambic dimeter is read
and 1076 where in M is ότοτοτοτοῖ ποποῖ [ototototoi popoi], of which the former Triclinius corrected, the latter I.
outside the meter, where undoubtedly a dochmius is to be restored: ὀτοτοτοῖ τοτοῖ [otototoi tototoi].
outside the verse, where more probable seems ἐὴ ἐὴ, ὀτοτοτοῖ τοτοῖ [e e, otototoi tototoi].
and in the antistrophe. For the former τοτοῖ [tototoi] in M in both places ποποῖ [popoi] is written, which I corrected.

οὐ [not] with adverbs and adverbial phrases.
On the particles οὐ μή [not... lest] (and οὔ τι μή, οὐδὲ μή, οὐδὲν μή), which are constructed with the aorist subjunctive or future indicative
For examples of οὐ [not] combined with any other particles, see under those particles. Most frequent is οὐ γάρ [for not]
οὐ [not] is usually placed before the word to which it belongs, as in the many places indicated above: more rarely it is placed after

οὐ [not] either repeated or combined with other negations of the same family makes a stronger negation.
